clue.text: Basic requirements met as sensible rate ordered

indicators.note: letters that are ordered are put into a new sequence, so the preceding words get rearranged

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A household budget meets its basic needs because someone set a sensible rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' is only a joining word between the definition and the fodder: BARE ESSENTIALS.
explanation.definitionFit: The bare essentials are the minimum things needed, exactly what basic requirements describes.

clue.text: Awfully slender, eh?  But manipulating the guidelines

definitions.note: a participle phrase for a verb phrase answer

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out in a disordered state

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a person is terribly thin, then turns to bending regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder runs across the punctuation: slender, eh and But together make BEND THE RULES.
explanation.definitionFit: To bend the rules is to stretch regulations to suit yourself without openly breaking them, a form of manipulation.

clue.text: About to manage a second showing

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Someone is about to organise a repeat screening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'About' gives its own letters and 'to manage' gives the rest: RERUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a repeat broadcast or performance, shown again after the original airing.

clue.text: Smitten with new name -- our journalist!

indicators.note: a new version of a word is a remade one, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written
ED is short for editor, the standard crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper boasts that its own reporter is besotted with some newly famous name.
explanation.walkthrough: ENAMOURED: a rearranged NAME, then OUR, then ED for editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enamoured means being filled with love or infatuation, the same state as smitten.

clue.text: Turn up with hesitation after scandal initially resulted in defamation

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows
after places the first two pieces behind the starting letter in the build

blocks.note: the opening letter of scandal
to turn up somewhere is to arrive or land
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A hesitant appearance after a scandal broke led to a libel case.
explanation.walkthrough: SLANDER is S + LAND + ER; 'Turn up' means arrive, not reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Slander is spoken defamation, false statements that damage someone's reputation.

clue.text: Bag a dance! Be a sport!

blocks.note: to bag something is to net or catch it
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Two cheerful exclamations urge someone to grab a dance and be a good sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be a sport' is an idiom for being obliging, but here 'a sport' is the definition, with 'Be' linking: NETBALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team game, popular in Britain and the Commonwealth, where players shoot a ball through a high hoop.

clue.text: I go first to the lavatory in a cold house

indicators.note: first asks for only the leading letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
the leading letter of go
loo is an informal British word for a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone insists on being first to the bathroom in a chilly home.
explanation.walkthrough: I + G + LOO gives IGLOO; 'I go first' reads as a claim of priority but is the first two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped shelter built from blocks of snow, literally a house made of cold material.

clue.text: US city scheme the German found for a Northerner

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
a scheme is a plan
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: An American urban project and a German organisation find a home for someone from the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: LA + PLAN + DER: LAPLANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A Laplander lives in Lapland, the region spanning the far north of Scandinavia and Russia.

clue.text: Opera girl

blocks.note: first meaning: Bellini's opera about a Druid priestess
second meaning: a female first name

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two meanings of the same name: NORMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a famous opera by Bellini and also a common woman's first name.

clue.text: Animal at stake -- run!

blocks.note: an ante is a stake put up in poker
to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: An animal's life is in danger and it is told to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At stake' reads as 'in danger', but 'at' is a link and 'stake' a poker term: ANTE + LOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a swift, slender hoofed mammal of Africa and Asia, a kind of animal.

clue.text: International sports side spilled talcum powder

indicators.note: something spilled is scattered about, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A national team has knocked over its talc in the changing room.
explanation.walkthrough: TALCUM POWDER rearranges to WORLD CUP TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A World Cup team is a national squad competing in an international tournament such as football's.

clue.text: Danced with zest, love to exercise daily initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of each of the two words before it

blocks.note: a tang is a sharp, zesty flavour
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
the first letters of exercise and daily

explanation.surface: Someone danced energetically, keen to keep up a daily exercise routine.
explanation.walkthrough: TANG + O + ED gives TANGOED; 'initially' covers both 'exercise' and 'daily'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have tangoed is to have performed the tango, the Argentine ballroom dance, so the past tense fits danced.

clue.text: A vocal majority at party find pear

indicators.note: a majority is most but not all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then cut short
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: A noisy majority of guests at a gathering discover a pear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vocal majority' reads like a political phrase; it means most of 'vocal', VOCA. A + VOCA + DO gives AVOCADO.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is often called an avocado pear in Britain because of its pear-like shape.

clue.text: Go into forbidden territory

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone trespasses onto land they have been told to keep off.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no explicit container word: the definition sits right against the two words that conceal it, a light Quiptic touch.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is simply to come or go into a place, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Herb, a product of a Spanish town

blocks.note: tarragon is an aromatic culinary herb
taken as written

explanation.surface: A herb is presented as a speciality produced in a Spanish town.
explanation.walkthrough: TARRAGON + A gives TARRAGONA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragona is a port city in Catalonia on Spain's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Poser after actor's part, for example

indicators.note: after places the first-named word behind the second in the build

blocks.note: an actor plays a role
a model poses for artists or photographers

explanation.surface: A poseur chases a part in a play, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' reads as a phrase, but 'for' is a link and 'example' the definition. ROLE + MODEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is someone whose behaviour others copy, a person set up as an example.

clue.text: Lunatic dream that led to his tea party

definitions.text: Lunatic dream that led to his tea party

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the letters that follow are scrambled wildly

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crazy dream produced a famous tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, Alice dreams the whole story, including the Mad Hatter's tea party; DREAM THAT rearranges to MAD HATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mad Hatter is the lunatic host of the tea party in Carroll's book, which Alice dreamed.

clue.text: Lie and rub without restraint

indicators.note: letters with no restraint are free to move, so they can be rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lounges around and scratches themselves, with nothing to hold them back.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue pictures a horse that will not be ridden: it lies down, rolls and rubs, with no tack on.
explanation.definitionFit: An unridable horse is one that refuses to carry a rider, behaving freely like an unbroken animal.

clue.text: Artillery attack

blocks.note: first meaning: a unit or group of big guns
second meaning: physical assault

explanation.walkthrough: Both words sound military, so it reads as one idea, but they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery is a set of artillery guns, and in law battery is the crime of physically striking someone.

clue.text: Two points given to sound sense and character

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how the next word is spoken, not its spelling

blocks.note: E and S are compass points, east and south
said, the word matches the end of the answer spelt with a C

explanation.surface: Someone is credited with a couple of good points for being level-headed and of good character.
explanation.walkthrough: ES plus a word pronounced like 'sense' gives ESSENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its fundamental nature, its intrinsic character.

clue.text: An old Greek style of celebration to Richard, but not hard

indicators.note: but not asks us to take away the word that follows from the name before it

blocks.note: a do is a party or celebration
taken as written before the cut
the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A party thrown for a man called Richard is in an ancient Greek fashion, but not a difficult one.
explanation.walkthrough: RICHARD without HARD leaves RIC; DO + RIC gives DORIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is the oldest and plainest of the classical Greek architectural orders.

clue.text: Shoulder decoration for man in the middle when peg's returned

indicators.note: in the middle places one piece inside the other
returned means sent back, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: a tee is the peg a golf ball sits on
a man's name

explanation.surface: A man stuck in the middle gets a decoration for his shoulder once a peg is given back.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf peg is the one a ball sits on; splitting its reversal two letters and one gives the outer pieces E and ET.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulet is an ornamental shoulder piece on a military or ceremonial uniform.

clue.text: Dreaded disease!

blocks.note: surface reading: an alarming, feared illness
setter's reading: the word always paired with it in the catchphrase from the Goon Show

explanation.walkthrough: 'The dreaded lurgi' is a British joke illness from the 1950s radio comedy The Goon Show, now used for any vague bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurgi is British slang for an unspecified, supposedly catching illness, always described as dreaded.

clue.text: Become fit, getting physique to a higher level

blocks.note: your shape is your body's form
up means towards a higher level

explanation.surface: Someone gets in condition, taking their body to the next level.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAPE + UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape up means to improve, including getting into better physical condition.

clue.text: The age to find a poetic muse

blocks.note: an era is an age
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to find the muse who inspired poets of the period.
explanation.walkthrough: ERA + TO gives ERATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek muse of lyric and love poetry, one of the nine Muses.

clue.text: Number 10 with the number of the Gospels

blocks.clueFragment: Number 10 with the number of the Gospels
blocks.note: surface reading: a sum involving a house number and the four Gospels

blocks.clueFragment: 10 with the number of the Gospels
blocks.note: setter's reading: ten added to the count of the Gospels, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John

explanation.surface: Downing Street gets a religious makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 10 suggests Downing Street, but this is simple addition: ten plus the four Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: Fourteen is the number reached by adding four to ten, so it is defined as a number.

clue.text: Wind up with drinks at some point

blocks.note: cups of tea are drinks
east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An evening will finish with a round of drinks eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' looks like 'finish', but it means to provoke. TEAS + E gives TEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind someone up is British slang for to tease or needle them deliberately.

clue.text: Relic of generations in airy mill -- home of Reformation

indicators.note: re-formation means forming again, so the letters are reassembled in a fresh order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An old relic is found in a breezy mill where the Reformation began.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes 'Reformation' look historical, but it is an anagram signal; 'of' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A family heirloom is a valued object handed down through several generations, a relic of a family's past.
